chapter: Chano Pozo, Town Hall and Charlie Parker
title: Working with Parker: no problems, always blaming himself
summary: Parker played on top of the band, catered to them, and always said he could do better.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: What about with your band though, did they understand that? Did they like it?

Well, because he played - he play on top of what we did. Is a different thing when he was playing, let's say, solos, that he come with some kind of idea, that was so progressive, that was more advanced that the people that was playing for him; but he catered to us and we catered to him. It was a complete understanding, without pride.
You never had a problem with Charlie Parker?
..... no, no, no, no, no, he was a gentleman.
and everytime that the session ended or the gig ended, everything was fine?

He would say, for his part, 'We could do better' or 'I could do better'. He never say, you could do better. 'I could do better than that, let's play again, please Machito, please'; 'Forgive me, but I think I could do better'. He always blamed himself. He never blamed the band because we was reading, we were reading what was written; so the problem was his problem, that he considered that he could do better. It was acceptable definitely for us and for everybody, but for him - that he was more advanced than anybody - he considered that he could do better.
